title: Experimental Chemistry I
source_note: Standard NUC-aligned Nigerian university 100L introductory chemistry practical curriculum: laboratory safety, basic apparatus and measurement, volumetric analysis fundamentals, simple qualitative tests, and basic separation techniques (filtration, crystallization, simple distillation).

questions.question: What is the first action a student should take immediately after a chemical splashes into their eye in the laboratory?
options: Wash the eye continuously with clean running water for at least 15 minutes
Rub the eye gently to remove the chemical
Wait to see if irritation develops before acting
questions.correct_answer: Wash the eye continuously with clean running water for at least 15 minutes
questions.explanation: Immediate and prolonged flushing with water dilutes and removes the chemical before it can cause serious damage; rubbing or delaying treatment can worsen injury.

questions.question: Which piece of glassware is most appropriate for accurately measuring and delivering a precise, variable volume of liquid during a titration?
questions.explanation: A burette has fine graduations and a stopcock that allow precise, controlled, variable delivery of liquid, which is essential for titrations.

questions.question: In a titration, what is the term for the substance whose concentration is being determined?
questions.explanation: The analyte is the unknown solution being analyzed, while the titrant is the solution of known concentration added from the burette.

questions.question: A student prepares a standard solution of sodium carbonate for use in acid-base titrations. What makes sodium carbonate suitable as a primary standard?
options: It is available in high purity, is stable, and has a well-defined molar mass
It is a strong base with an unlimited shelf life in any form
It reacts instantly with any indicator to give a sharp colour change
It is cheaper than all other standardizing agents
questions.correct_answer: It is available in high purity, is stable, and has a well-defined molar mass
questions.explanation: A primary standard must be obtainable in a pure, stable, non-hygroscopic form with an accurately known molar mass so that solutions of exactly known concentration can be prepared by direct weighing.

questions.question: Which piece of apparatus is used to deliver a fixed, precise volume of liquid, such as 25.00 cm3, in a single measurement?
questions.explanation: A volumetric pipette is calibrated to deliver one fixed, highly accurate volume, unlike a burette which delivers variable volumes.

questions.question: Why should a burette be rinsed with the titrant solution before it is filled for use, even after washing with distilled water?
options: To remove residual water that would dilute and alter the concentration of the titrant
To make the glass shinier for easier reading
To warm the burette to room temperature
questions.correct_answer: To remove residual water that would dilute and alter the concentration of the titrant
questions.explanation: Any water left in the burette would dilute the titrant, changing its effective concentration and introducing error into the titration result.

questions.question: What is the correct procedure for reading the volume on a burette containing an aqueous solution?
options: Read the bottom of the meniscus at eye level
Read the top of the meniscus while looking downward
Read the volume from above the burette
Read the nearest whole millilitre only
questions.correct_answer: Read the bottom of the meniscus at eye level
questions.explanation: For most aqueous solutions, the meniscus curves downward, and reading at eye level from the bottom of the curve avoids parallax error.

questions.question: Phenolphthalein is colourless in acidic solution and pink in basic solution. In which type of titration would it be an unsuitable indicator?
options: Titration of a weak base against a strong acid
Titration of a strong acid against a strong base
Titration of a weak acid against a strong base
None of these; it works in all titrations equally well
questions.correct_answer: Titration of a weak base against a strong acid
questions.explanation: The equivalence point of a weak base-strong acid titration is acidic (below pH 7), which falls outside phenolphthalein's colour-change range (pH 8.2-10), making methyl orange more suitable.

questions.question: Which separation technique is used to separate an insoluble solid from a liquid using a porous medium?
questions.explanation: Filtration passes a mixture through filter paper or another porous medium, retaining the insoluble solid while the liquid passes through as filtrate.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of recrystallization in purifying a solid?
options: To remove soluble impurities by exploiting differences in solubility at different temperatures
To change the chemical identity of the compound
To evaporate all the solvent so the solid becomes a gas
To increase the melting point of the substance artificially
questions.correct_answer: To remove soluble impurities by exploiting differences in solubility at different temperatures
questions.explanation: Recrystallization dissolves the impure solid in a hot solvent and allows pure crystals to form on cooling, leaving impurities dissolved in the mother liquor.

questions.question: Which technique would best separate two miscible liquids with significantly different boiling points?
questions.explanation: Simple distillation separates miscible liquids based on differences in boiling point: the liquid with the lower boiling point vaporizes first and is collected after condensation.

questions.question: A student determines that an unknown solid melts sharply at 132-133 degC, matching the literature value for benzoic acid. What does the sharp, narrow melting range suggest?
questions.explanation: Impurities generally lower and broaden the melting point range; a sharp melting range close to the literature value indicates a pure sample.

questions.question: What does it mean if an unknown solid shows a melting point range of 110-125 degC instead of a sharp single value?
options: The solid is a pure element
The solid has an unusually high density
questions.explanation: A broad, depressed melting range is a classic indication of impurity, since foreign substances disrupt the crystal lattice and lower the melting point.

questions.question: Which instrument is used to measure the mass of a chemical sample accurately in the laboratory?
questions.explanation: An analytical balance is designed to measure mass with high precision, often to four decimal places in grams.

questions.question: A student needs to prepare 250 cm3 of a standard solution from a weighed solid. Which apparatus must be used to make up the solution to the exact final volume?
questions.explanation: A volumetric flask has a single calibration mark and is designed to contain one precise volume when filled to the mark, essential for accurate standard solution preparation.

questions.question: 0.265 g of anhydrous sodium carbonate (molar mass 106 g/mol) is dissolved and made up to 250 cm3. What is the concentration of the solution in mol/dm3?
questions.explanation: Moles = 0.265/106 = 0.0025 mol; concentration = 0.0025 mol / 0.250 dm3 = 0.01 mol/dm3.

questions.question: In an acid-base titration, 25.0 cm3 of 0.100 mol/dm3 NaOH exactly neutralizes 20.0 cm3 of HCl. What is the concentration of the HCl?
questions.explanation: Moles NaOH = 0.025 dm3 x 0.100 mol/dm3 = 0.0025 mol; since the mole ratio is 1:1, moles HCl = 0.0025 mol; concentration = 0.0025/0.020 = 0.125 mol/dm3.

questions.question: Which simple qualitative test is used to confirm the presence of carbon dioxide gas?
options: It turns blue litmus paper red instantly
It produces a pop sound with a lit splint
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide reacts with calcium hydroxide (limewater) to form insoluble calcium carbonate, causing a milky/cloudy appearance, the standard confirmatory test.

questions.question: A glowing splint relights when placed in a test tube of gas. Which gas is present?
questions.explanation: Oxygen supports combustion strongly enough to relight a glowing splint, which is the standard test for its presence.

questions.question: Which gas produces a characteristic 'pop' sound when tested with a lighted splint?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen gas combusts rapidly with a distinctive pop sound when ignited by a lit splint, the classic confirmatory test.

questions.question: Damp red litmus paper turns blue when exposed to a colourless gas with a pungent smell. Which gas is most likely present?
questions.explanation: Ammonia is an alkaline gas that turns damp red litmus paper blue, and its pungent smell is characteristic.

questions.question: What safety precaution must be observed when diluting concentrated sulfuric acid with water?
options: Always add the acid slowly to water, never water to acid
Always add water slowly to the acid
Mix them at equal speed simultaneously
Heat both liquids first before mixing
questions.correct_answer: Always add the acid slowly to water, never water to acid
questions.explanation: Adding acid to water allows the large heat of dilution to be absorbed by the larger volume of water; adding water to concentrated acid can cause violent spattering and burns.

questions.question: Which laboratory equipment protects the eyes from chemical splashes and should be worn throughout practical sessions?
questions.explanation: Safety goggles form a seal around the eyes and are specifically designed to protect against chemical splashes, unlike a lab coat or gloves which protect skin.

questions.question: What is the correct first-aid action for a minor acid spill on the skin?
options: Wash the affected area immediately with plenty of water
Apply a base such as sodium hydroxide directly to neutralize it
Cover the area with a dry cloth without washing
questions.correct_answer: Wash the affected area immediately with plenty of water
questions.explanation: Flushing with plenty of water dilutes and removes the acid quickly; applying another chemical like a strong base can cause an additional exothermic reaction and worsen injury.

questions.question: In writing a laboratory report, what is the primary purpose of the 'discussion' section?
options: To interpret the results, explain sources of error, and relate findings to theory
To list only the raw data collected
To state the list of apparatus used
To describe the safety precautions taken
questions.correct_answer: To interpret the results, explain sources of error, and relate findings to theory
questions.explanation: The discussion section is where the experimenter analyzes results, compares them with expected/theoretical values, and accounts for discrepancies or errors.

questions.question: Which term describes an error that consistently occurs in the same direction, such as an incorrectly calibrated balance always reading high?
questions.explanation: A systematic error is a consistent, repeatable bias in the same direction, often caused by faulty equipment or a flawed procedure, and it can be corrected once identified.

questions.question: What does 'accuracy' mean in the context of experimental measurements, as distinct from 'precision'?
options: How close a measured value is to the true or accepted value
How closely repeated measurements agree with each other
How many decimal places an instrument can display
How quickly a measurement can be taken
questions.correct_answer: How close a measured value is to the true or accepted value
questions.explanation: Accuracy refers to closeness to the true value, while precision refers to the reproducibility/consistency of repeated measurements, which may or may not be close to the true value.

questions.question: Which piece of apparatus would be used to gently heat a liquid in a test tube over a Bunsen flame in a school/undergraduate lab?
questions.explanation: A test tube holder allows a test tube to be held safely over a flame without direct contact with the hot glass, preventing burns.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a wash bottle containing distilled water in volumetric analysis?
options: To rinse apparatus and wash down the sides of flasks to ensure all reagent is included in the reaction
To dilute the titrant to half its concentration
To act as the primary titrant
To clean spilled acid on the bench
questions.correct_answer: To rinse apparatus and wash down the sides of flasks to ensure all reagent is included in the reaction
questions.explanation: Rinsing with distilled water ensures that no reagent clinging to the walls of the apparatus is left out of the reaction, which would introduce error.

questions.question: A colourless gas turns acidified potassium dichromate paper from orange to green. Which gas is indicated?
questions.explanation: Sulfur dioxide is a reducing gas that reduces the orange dichromate(VI) ion to the green chromium(III) ion, a standard confirmatory test.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the purpose of a control experiment in a chemistry practical?
options: To provide a baseline for comparison so that the effect of the variable being tested can be isolated
To repeat the main experiment exactly to save time
To use a different chemical entirely from the main experiment
To skip the need for accurate measurements
questions.correct_answer: To provide a baseline for comparison so that the effect of the variable being tested can be isolated
questions.explanation: A control experiment keeps all other conditions constant except the variable of interest, allowing the effect of that one variable to be identified clearly.

questions.question: Which of these is the correct order of steps when standardizing a burette before a titration?
options: Rinse with distilled water, then rinse with titrant, then fill and remove air bubbles from the tip
Fill directly from the reagent bottle without rinsing
Rinse only with titrant and never with water
Fill the burette, then check for air bubbles only if the titration fails
questions.correct_answer: Rinse with distilled water, then rinse with titrant, then fill and remove air bubbles from the tip
questions.explanation: Proper preparation requires cleaning with water first, then rinsing with the titrant to remove residual water, then filling and ensuring no air bubbles are trapped in the tip, which would cause volume errors.
